blueprint.coverage_deficit_addressed: Genetic modifiers of motor-neuron disease severity

item.vignette: Two brothers have genetically confirmed 5q spinal muscular atrophy caused by the same homozygous SMN1 deletion. The older brother developed profound weakness and respiratory failure in infancy. The younger brother did not develop proximal weakness until early childhood and can still sit independently. Genetic testing shows that the younger brother has four copies of SMN2, whereas the older brother has two.
item.lead_in: Which mechanism best explains the milder phenotype in the younger brother?

options.A: Skewed X-chromosome inactivation preserves motor-neuron function
options.B: Paternal imprinting activates a normally silent SMN1 allele
options.C: Contraction of a pathogenic trinucleotide repeat increases SMN protein production
options.D: Additional SMN2 copies produce more functional survival motor neuron protein
options.E: A lower proportion of mutant mitochondrial DNA reduces tissue heteroplasmy

item.tested_construct: SMN2 copy number as a severity modifier in spinal muscular atrophy

explanation.key_explanation: SMN1 loss causes spinal muscular atrophy. SMN2 can generate a small amount of functional SMN protein; therefore, a higher SMN2 copy number partially compensates for SMN1 deficiency and is generally associated with a milder, later-onset phenotype.

distractor_explanations.A: SMA is autosomal recessive, so X-inactivation does not explain intrafamilial severity differences.
distractor_explanations.B: SMN1 disease is not explained by a parent-of-origin imprinting mechanism.
distractor_explanations.C: SMA is caused by SMN1 loss, not a pathogenic trinucleotide-repeat expansion.
distractor_explanations.D: Correct. More SMN2 copies generally increase functional SMN protein and ameliorate disease severity.
distractor_explanations.E: SMA is a nuclear-gene disorder rather than a mitochondrial heteroplasmy disorder.

explanation.educational_objective: Recognize SMN2 copy number as an important modifier of spinal muscular atrophy severity because additional copies generate more functional SMN protein.

evidence_map.claim: 5q SMA is inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern caused by SMN1 mutations.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: X-inactivation is not the relevant modifier.

evidence_map.claim: SMA severity is modified by SMN2 dosage rather than activation of an imprinted SMN1 allele.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: The same homozygous SMN1 deletion is present in both siblings.

evidence_map.claim: SMN1 deletion, not a trinucleotide-repeat expansion, is the defining molecular lesion in most SMA.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: Repeat contraction cannot explain the observed genotype.

evidence_map.claim: More SMN2 copies usually produce more functional SMN protein and are associated with milder, later-onset SMA.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: Directly explains the younger brother's four-copy SMN2 genotype and milder course.

evidence_map.claim: 5q SMA is a nuclear SMN1/SMN2 disorder, so mitochondrial heteroplasmy is not the disease mechanism.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: The stem provides a nuclear-gene copy-number modifier.
